newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Fighting resumes in Cambodian capital at dawn.
newsitem.headline: Fighting resumes in Cambodian capital at dawn.

text.p: Fighting between troops loyal to Cambodia's rival prime ministers resumed in the Cambodian capital at dawn on Sunday as the country's first prime minister accused his rival of attempting a coup.

Sustained shelling could be heard coming from the vicinity of the well-fortified compound close to the city centre where top generals and officials loyal to First Prime Minister Price Norodom Ranariddh live. The area was the scene of fighting between the two sides the previous day, in which at least four people were killed and some 20 wounded.
The fighting began again shortly before a curfew imposed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. came to an end after a mainly quiet night.

Ranariddh, who is in France, released a statement there saying the action against his forces was a coup d'etat. "We consider that what is currently happening in Phnom Penh is a coup d'etat perpetuated by (second Prime Minister) Mr Hun Sen," said a statement released in Paris in the name of Ranariddh.

In a second statement issued hours later in Paris, where he was said to be visiting family, Ranariddh declared he had become head of Cambodia's only legitimate government as a result of the alleged coup attempt.

Hun Sen's troops blocked main thoroughfares in Phnom Penh on Saturday and armoured personnel carriers were stationed at strategic locations around the city as fighting was also reported in some other parts of the country. The two prime ministers head a deadlocked coalition government and have had a long-standing row over power-sharing.
